passages.text: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son.
passages.sermon: Nahash was the king of the Ammonites.\r\nNahash died.\r\nHis son became king after him.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת נָחָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to console Hanun concerning his father. But when David’s servants arrived in the land of the Ammonites to console him, the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
David wanted to show kindness to Hanun.
Hanun was the son of Nahash.
Nahash had shown kindness to David.
David decided to repay this kindness.
David sent messengers to Hanun.
David sent them to comfort Hanun about his father’s death.
David’s servants went to the land of the Ammonites.
They went to Hanun to comfort him.
The princes of the Ammonites spoke to Hanun.
They questioned David’s intentions.
They asked Hanun if David really honored his father by sending comforters.
They suggested another reason for the visit.
They said David’s servants came to explore the land.
They said the servants came to spy on the land.
They said the servants came to overthrow the land.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ חֶ֣סֶד׀ עִם־ חָנ֣וּן בֶּן־ נָחָ֗שׁ כִּֽי־ עָשָׂ֨ה אָבִ֤יו עִמִּי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛יד מַלְאָכִ֖ים לְנַחֲמ֣וֹ עַל־ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֜יד אֶל־ אֶ֧רֶץ בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֛וֹן אֶל־ חָנ֖וּן לְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃ וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵי־ עַמּ֜וֹן לְחָנ֗וּן הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤יד אֶת־ אָבִ֙יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־ שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַחֲמִ֑ים הֲלֹ֡א בַּ֠עֲבוּר לַחְקֹ֨ר וְלַהֲפֹ֤ךְ וּלְרַגֵּל֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ בָּ֥אוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ׃פ

passages.text: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
passages.sermon:
Hanun was the new king of the Ammonites.
David sent his servants to Hanun.
Hanun took David’s servants.
Hanun shaved off their beards.
Hanun cut their garments at the hips.
Hanun sent the servants away.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חָנ֜וּן אֶת־ עַבְדֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ וַֽיְגַלְּחֵ֔ם וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת אֶת־ מַדְוֵיהֶ֛ם בַּחֵ֖צִי עַד־ הַמִּפְשָׂעָ֑ה וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: When someone came and told David about his men, he sent messengers to meet them, since the men had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David’s servants had been sent to Hanun, king of the Ammonites.
Hanun humiliated David’s servants.
Someone told David what happened to his men.
David heard about his men’s humiliation.
David sent messengers to meet his men.
The men were very ashamed.
David was concerned for his men.
David spoke to his men.
David said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back.”
David said, “After your beards grow, return home.”
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ וַיַּגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֤יד עַל־ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּי־ הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites saw that David was angry with them.
Hanun was the king of the Ammonites.
Hanun and the Ammonites wanted to protect themselves.
They sent one thousand talents of silver.
They used this silver to hire help.
They hired chariots and horsemen.
They hired these fighters from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
passages.original: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִֽתְבָּאֲשׁ֖וּ עִם־ דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חָ֠נוּן וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן אֶ֣לֶף כִּכַּר־ כֶּ֗סֶף לִשְׂכֹּ֣ר לָ֠הֶם מִן־ אֲרַ֨ם נַהֲרַ֜יִם וּמִן־ אֲרַ֤ם מַעֲכָה֙ וּמִצּוֹבָ֔ה רֶ֖כֶב וּפָרָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba while the Ammonites came from their cities and marched out for battle.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites hired thirty-two thousand chariots.
They also hired the king of Maacah and his army.
The king of Maacah and his troops came.
They camped near Medeba.
The Ammonites gathered from their cities.
The Ammonites came out to fight in battle.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂכְּר֣וּ לָהֶ֡ם שְׁנַיִם֩ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף רֶ֗כֶב וְאֶת־ מֶ֤לֶךְ מַעֲכָה֙ וְאֶת־ עַמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י מֵידְבָ֑א וּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן נֶאֶסְפוּ֙ מֵעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃פ

passages.text: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David heard about the situation.
David acted quickly.
David sent Joab.
Joab was the commander of his army.
David also sent the entire army of mighty men.
The mighty men were strong and brave warriors.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶת־ יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־ צָבָ֖א הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites were a people who opposed Israel.
The Ammonites marched out from their city.
They prepared for battle at the entrance to the city.
Several kings had come to help the Ammonites.
These kings did not join the Ammonites at the city entrance.
The kings stayed by themselves in the open country.
passages.original: וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיַּֽעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה פֶּ֣תַח הָעִ֑יר וְהַמְּלָכִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֔אוּ לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab saw the enemy in front of him.
Joab saw the enemy behind him.
Joab understood that he was surrounded.
Joab chose the best soldiers from Israel.
Joab arranged these chosen men to face the Arameans.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹאָ֗ב כִּֽי־ הָיְתָ֧ה פְנֵי־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו פָּנִ֣ים וְאָח֑וֹר וַיִּבְחַ֗ר מִכָּל־ בָּחוּר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ לִקְרַ֥את אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: And he placed the rest of the forces under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab had a brother named Abishai.
Joab took the rest of the soldiers.
Joab put these soldiers under Abishai’s command.
Abishai led these men.
Abishai arranged them for battle.
Abishai prepared to fight the Ammonites.
passages.original: וְאֵת֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם נָתַ֕ן בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֑יו וַיַּ֣עַרְכ֔וּ לִקְרַ֖את בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander of Israel’s army.
Joab spoke to his brother Abishai.
Joab said, “If the Arameans are stronger than I am, you must help me.
If the Ammonites are stronger than you, I will help you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִם־ תֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ אֲרָ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתָ לִּ֖י לִתְשׁוּעָ֑הס וְאִם־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֛וֹן יֶֽחֶזְק֥וּ מִמְּךָ֖ וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
He spoke to his brother Abishai.
Joab said, “Be strong.”
He said, “Let us show courage.”
He said, “We must fight for our people.”
He said, “We must fight for the cities that belong to our God.”
He said, “The LORD will do what is good in His sight.”
passages.original: חֲזַ֤ק וְנִֽתְחַזְּקָה֙ בְּעַד־ עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab led his soldiers forward.
They went to fight the Arameans.
The Arameans saw Joab and his troops.
The Arameans ran away from Joab.
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ יוֹאָ֜ב וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֛וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיָּנ֖וּסוּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Joab’s brother Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled.
The Ammonites also fled.
They ran away from Abishai, who was Joab’s brother.
The Ammonites entered the city.
Joab returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי־ נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם וַיָּנ֣וּסוּ גַם־ הֵ֗ם מִפְּנֵי֙ אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָעִ֑ירָה וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

passages.text: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
passages.sermon:
The Arameans saw that Israel had defeated them.
The Arameans sent messengers.
The messengers brought more Aramean soldiers.
These soldiers came from beyond the Euphrates River.
Shophach led these soldiers.
Shophach was the commander of Hadadezer’s army.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֗ם כִּ֣י נִגְּפוּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת־ אֲרָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשׁוֹפַ֛ךְ שַׂר־ צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, advanced toward the Arameans, and arrayed for battle against them. When David lined up to engage them in battle, they fought against him.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Someone reported news to David.
David heard the report.
David gathered all the people of Israel.
David led Israel across the Jordan River.
David advanced toward the Arameans.
David arranged his army for battle against the Arameans.
David prepared to fight the Arameans.
The Arameans fought against David.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗יד וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲרֹ֨ךְ דָּוִ֜יד לִקְרַ֤את אֲרָם֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
The Arameans fought against Israel.
The Arameans saw Israel’s strength.
The Arameans ran away from Israel.
David and his army chased the Arameans.
David killed seven thousand Aramean charioteers.
David killed forty thousand Aramean foot soldiers.
Shophach was the commander of the Aramean army.
David killed Shophach.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜יד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וְאֵ֛ת שׁוֹפַ֥ךְ שַֽׂר־ הַצָּבָ֖א הֵמִֽית׃

passages.text: When Hadadezer’s subjects saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore.
passages.sermon:
Hadadezer was a king.
He had subjects who served him.
These subjects saw that Israel defeated them.
They saw their defeat clearly.
They decided to make peace with David.
They became David’s servants.
The Arameans were these people.
The Arameans refused to help the Ammonites again.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֞וּ עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥ימוּ עִם־ דָּוִ֖יד וַיַּֽעַבְדֻ֑הוּ וְלֹא־ אָבָ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת־ בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֖וֹן עֽוֹד׃פ
